newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban say 225 women punished for improper dress.
newsitem.headline: Taleban say 225 women punished for improper dress.

text.p: Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban militia said it had meted out undisclosed punishment to 225 women on Thursday for violating its rules on clothing.

"Today 225 women were punished as they did not respect the Islamic sharia (law)," Taleban-controlled Sharia Radio said. "We announced once again that all women should wear the burqa and veil and respect sharia or face punishment."
In the past women have been beaten in public for alleged violations of Islamic dress codes.

The radio, monitored in the Pakistani capital Islamabad, said several young men who had failed to grow beards or who had trimmed them in violation of Taleban edicts had also been punished and dismissed from their jobs.

It said a Taleban shura, or council, for promoting good and banning evil had met in Kabul on Thursday to discuss the issue. "The meeting said that men should grow thick beards and small moustaches within one and a half months," the radio reported.

The radio broadcast a warning on Wednesday that wearing the long, shapeless chador robe did not meet Islamic standards of women's dress. It insisted that they wear the burqa, a head-to-toe robe which conceals the face with a cloth mesh.
Confusingly, the latest crackdown followed a message on Tuesday from Taleban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar ordering his men to deal more leniently with the people of Kabul.
The Taleban, who captured Kabul on September 27 from forces loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani, have vowed to implement strict sharia law throughout Afghanistan.
